content: Diabetes Australia NSW is the foremost charity in Australia dedicated to addressing diabetes and is recognized as the third oldest diabetes organization globally. It serves as the regional counterpart to the American Diabetes Association and Diabetes UK. Established in 1937 and headquartered in Sydney, New South Wales (NSW), the organization is committed to assisting Australians living with diabetes by mitigating the impact of this rapidly growing chronic disease on their lives. As a non-profit, non-governmental organization, Diabetes Australia NSW relies on funding from its members and donations. All funds raised are allocated to research, educational initiatives, public awareness campaigns, and advocacy efforts. The organization operates a call center that handles over 600 phone calls daily, where trained staff provide personalized and practical support to individuals with diabetes and their caregivers. Additionally, Diabetes Australia NSW manages the Australian government’s National Diabetes Services Scheme, which offers subsidized products to Australians living with diabetes. Diabetes Australia NSW is part of a federation comprising twelve organizations, including the eight State and Territory Associations of Diabetes Australia, the Australian Diabetes Society, the Australian Diabetes Educators Association, the Kellion Diabetes Foundation, and the Diabetes Research Foundation Western Australia. Diabetes Statistics in Australia Over three million Australians are affected by diabetes or pre-diabetes. Diabetes is the fastest-growing chronic disease in the country and ranks as the sixth leading cause of death by disease in Australia. One in four Australian adults has either diabetes or impaired glucose metabolism. A new diabetes diagnosis occurs every seven minutes in Australia. In 2000-01, the diabetes-related death rate among Indigenous Australians was nearly 15 times higher than that of non-Indigenous Australians. Certain overseas-born Australians exhibit a higher prevalence of diabetes compared to those born in Australia. Diabetes in New South Wales (NSW) More than 542,000 people in NSW have diabetes, yet half of them remain undiagnosed. The prevalence of diabetes in NSW has surged by 300% over the past decade. The number of individuals with type 2 diabetes, often referred to as a lifestyle disease, has doubled within just five years. The incidence of type 2 diabetes in children is increasing at a rate of 5-10% annually. Type 1 diabetes in children is rising at a rate of 3% per year.
